boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented Simpson study environments, from library workrooms to residence-hall lounges.

cards.title: Dunn Library Group Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Dunn Library, Simpson College
cards.notes: Bring a project group and use a dedicated room for shared screens, drafts, and discussion; confirm room availability with the library before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Dedicated library rooms for team projects and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson states that Dunn Library features group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located in Dunn Library; consult library staff for current room-use arrangements.

cards.title: Dunn Library Individual Carrels
cards.subtitle: Dunn Library, Simpson College
cards.notes: Choose an individual carrel when you need a defined personal workstation, then keep reference materials close by in the library’s study environment.
cards.short_summary: Individual workstations inside Simpson’s renovated library.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson lists individual carrels among the study spaces at Dunn Library.
cards.access_notes: Located in Dunn Library during facility hours; follow library space-use guidance.

cards.entity_name: Dunn Library Third-Floor Quiet Collaborative Spaces
cards.title: Third-Floor Quiet Collaborative Spaces
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Dunn Library
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for a quieter collaborative setting, useful for low-volume partner work while staying near archival research resources.
cards.short_summary: A quieter, upper-floor setting for collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson identifies quiet collaborative spaces on Dunn Library’s third floor.
cards.access_notes: Third floor of Dunn Library; library lists term and summer facility hours on its page.

cards.title: Dunn Library Collaborative Spaces
cards.subtitle: Dunn Library, Simpson College
cards.notes: Use the library’s collaborative areas for a working session that needs conversation and shared materials; select a group room if you need more separation.
cards.short_summary: Open collaborative study areas throughout Dunn Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson says Dunn Library includes other collaborative spaces in addition to its group rooms and carrels.
cards.access_notes: Located in Dunn Library; use the space in accordance with current library guidance.

cards.entity_name: Joseph W. Walt Research Library & College Archives
cards.title: Walt Research Library & College Archives
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Dunn Library
cards.notes: Plan an archival research session around a specific question, then contact the archives in advance because its materials are used in-house by appointment.
cards.short_summary: Appointment-based primary-source research on Simpson’s third floor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Walt Research Library & College Archives is on Dunn Library’s third floor, and its materials are available for in-house use by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Materials are not browsable and may be used in-house by appointment only; email or call the archives first.

cards.title: Dunn Library South Entrance Patio
cards.subtitle: South entrance, Dunn Library
cards.notes: Take portable reading or a laptop outside to the patio by Dunn’s south entrance, then move indoors if weather or library needs change.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor patio attached to Simpson’s reimagined library.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson reports an outdoor patio by Dunn Library’s south entrance.
cards.source_title: Renovation of Dunn Library Lights up Learning
cards.access_notes: Outdoor seating by the south entrance; availability is weather-dependent.

cards.title: Kresge Hall Lounge/Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Lower, first, and second floors, Kresge Hall
cards.notes: If you live in Kresge, use the lounge/study areas on the lower, first, or second floor for a change from your room between classes.
cards.short_summary: Multiple residential lounge/study areas within Kresge Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson lists lounge/study areas on Kresge Hall’s lower, first, and second floors.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall space; building entry uses card access and is intended for its residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Barker Hall Lower-Level Lounge/Study Area
cards.subtitle: Lower level, Barker Hall
cards.notes: Barker residents can set up in the lower-level lounge/study area for a focused session close to their hall’s laundry and shared facilities.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level residential lounge and study setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson lists a lounge/study area on the lower level of Barker Hall.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall space; building entry uses card access and is intended for its residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Buxton Hall Lounge/Study Area
cards.subtitle: Buxton Hall, Simpson College
cards.notes: Buxton residents can work in the hall’s lounge/study area, then use the nearby computer room if their assignment calls for a campus workstation.
cards.short_summary: A residential study lounge paired with a first-floor computer room.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson lists a lounge/study area and a first-floor computer room among Buxton Hall’s amenities.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall amenities are intended for Buxton residents and authorized guests.

cards.title: Picken Hall First-Floor Study Area
cards.subtitle: First floor, Picken Hall
cards.notes: Picken residents can use the first-floor study area for a nearby work block, with a computer room in the same hall when desktop access is useful.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor residential study area with a computer room nearby.
cards.evidence_claim: Simpson lists a first-floor study area and computer room as amenities of Picken Hall.
cards.access_notes: Residence-hall amenities are intended for Picken residents and authorized guests.
